leading_positions.synthesis: Three of eight members include palladium-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling in their preferred configuration (Somfai and Zou as the sole part, Linke as one of two parts). All three name Buchwald and Hartwig and now exclude Kosugi (Zou moved from three names to two after the opening). They share the argument that the mechanism and ligand design are well understood and that three decades of independent use give it the strongest validation on the list. What is not shared is how far the 2010 cross-coupling prize closes the area: Aqvist, Aili and Chabes raise it as a novelty or overlap concern, and Zou and Somfai answer that C-N bond formation required its own ligand and mechanistic solutions. Aqvist and Aili describe it as the least contested on maturity and attribution, a safe fallback, but not necessarily first.

Three members include programmable DNA base editing in their preferred configuration (Chabes as the sole part, Brzezinski and Linke as one of two parts). They agree that it is a defined deaminase reaction directed to one nucleotide without a double-strand break, reproduced independently and already in clinical use. They differ on laureates: Chabes proposes Liu, Komor and Gaudelli, while Brzezinski and Linke propose Liu alone, partly so that a second part fits within the three-laureate limit. Somfai questions whether the novelty is chemistry or protein engineering close to the 2020 genome-editing prize; Aqvist and Zou list it as an alternative.

Two members prefer ionizable lipid nanoparticles as a single-part prize, and it is the item most often cited as having the strongest clinical validation (approved siRNA therapy and mRNA vaccines). Both name Cullis and Hope, but the third name differs: Anderson (Aili) versus Madden (Sparr), with MacLachlan and Langer also credited by others. Aili and Sparr argue that the 2023 Medicine prize recognized the cargo, not the delivery chemistry. Aqvist, Chabes, Brzezinski, Somfai and Zou all regard attribution as unresolved, and several hold it as an alternative or would support it only with an agreed narrow citation.

One member (Aqvist) prefers targeted protein degradation, with Crews, Deshaies and Handa, as a new pharmacological modality (concept plus the cereblon mechanism). Aili, Sparr and Somfai list it as an alternative, and Linke, Brzezinski, Zou and Chabes discuss it but do not prefer it. All who comment cite the absence of an approved degrader and an attribution split (Crews and Deshaies versus Handa and Ito, with Ciulli, Sakamoto and Gray also named) as the obstacles.

Only Brzezinski prefers long-range electron transfer through proteins (Gray and Winkler), and only as the first of two parts alongside B008. He notes that no other member ranked it first and that it is close to his own field. Sparr questions whether it adds enough beyond the 1992 Marcus prize.

areas_of_agreement: Every member who evaluated the biology-facing candidates agrees that attribution is the main obstacle for B016, B009 and B067, and that a three-laureate limit forces cuts of contributors with real claims.
Somfai, Zou, Linke and Chabes agree that Buchwald and Hartwig carry B011, and all members who discuss Kosugi treat his tin-amide work as a precursor rather than a co-discovery.

No member rejects B008 or B011 on the grounds of scientific quality; the objections to each concern overlap with an earlier prize (2020 genome editing, 2010 cross-coupling) and, for B008, the number of laureates.
Several members, including Aqvist, Brzezinski and Zou, state that clinical maturity matters, and that no degrader has yet been widely approved.
B003 (phase separation) and B067 (nanopores) were each lowered or set aside by their own proponents, Sparr and Linke, on maturity and attribution grounds.
scientific_disputes: Whether base editing is a distinct chemical invention (direct base conversion without a break, with an engineered DNA adenine deaminase) or a protein-engineering follow-on to the 2020 CRISPR prize (Linke and Chabes versus Somfai, with Aqvist and Brzezinski raising the overlap).

Whether C-N cross-coupling is a new concept requiring its own ligand and mechanistic solutions or a continuation of the 2010 palladium cross-coupling prize (Somfai, Zou, Linke versus the concern raised by Aqvist, Aili and Chabes).

Whether ionizable lipid nanoparticles are a chemical discovery (pKa-tuned design and lipid phase behaviour) or pharmaceutical formulation, and how far the 2023 Medicine prize overlaps the delivery chemistry.
Whether PROTACs (designed heterobifunctional molecules) and cereblon molecular glues (a mechanism found after the fact) form one achievement or two (Aqvist, Somfai, Brzezinski).
Whether the cereblon work is new chemistry or mechanism-of-action biology (Somfai).
attribution_disputes: B008: Liu alone (Aqvist, Brzezinski, Linke) versus Liu, Komor and Gaudelli (Aili, Chabes in the shortlist proposals), and whether Nishida and Kondo's concurrent cytidine-deaminase work deserves a place or only a mention.
B016: the third name beside Cullis and Hope is Anderson (Aili), Madden (Sparr) or MacLachlan, with Langer and the lipidoid line and industrial SNALP development also in question.
B011: Buchwald and Hartwig only (Somfai, Zou after change, Linke) versus adding Kosugi, as Zou did at the opening; Somfai has not verified the priority dates for Kosugi and Migita.
B009: Crews, Deshaies and Handa (Aqvist, Aili, Linke's ranking) versus Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli (Brzezinski, Chabes, Sparr in the shortlist proposals), with Sakamoto, Ito and Gray also named.
B067: Branton, Deamer, Bayley, Kasianowicz and Akeson are all credited and Linke and Sparr proposed different three-name sets; Aqvist and Chabes ask who made the decisive step.
maturity_disputes: B009: no degrader is widely approved, so the clinical payoff is still pending (raised by Aqvist himself, Aili, Brzezinski, Somfai and Zou).
B008: clinical record is short, and bystander and off-target deamination are open (Chabes, Brzezinski, Linke).
B003: physiological relevance of condensates versus in vitro droplets is contested (Sparr, Brzezinski, Zou, Linke).
B027: whether a decades-old mechanistic result is still open for recognition after the 1992 Marcus prize (Brzezinski, Sparr).
The two-part B011 plus B008 configuration combines a mature 1990s method with a field still in early clinical development (Linke).
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Brzezinski notes that B027 is close to his own research on electron and proton transfer and says he has tried to discount possible bias.
Sparr and Aili note topical overlap between their lipid, membrane and nanoparticle work and B016 and B003, which both describe as expertise and not a recusal issue.
Brzezinski and Zou are Stockholm University colleagues, and Linke, Somfai and Sparr are Lund colleagues; no member reports that a shortlisted candidate is connected to these institutions.
The chair (Linke) is a physicist whose own opening first choice was B067; he has lowered it and reports no personal or institutional tie to any shortlisted candidate.
questions_for_round2: For B008: is the invention best credited to Liu alone, or to Liu, Komor and Gaudelli, and what exactly is chemically new relative to the 2020 CRISPR prize and the concurrent Nishida and Kondo work?

For B011: what did the 1994-1995 work supply that the 1983 Kosugi tin-amide coupling lacked, and does the 2010 prize make a C-N coupling citation look like a continuation? Somfai is asked to answer as the specialist.
For B016: can the committee agree on one narrowly defined achievement and a defensible three names, and if so which: Anderson, Madden or MacLachlan beside Cullis and Hope?
For B009: has the clinical record reached the point where a principle is validated rather than promising, and can PROTACs and molecular glues be written as one citation? Aqvist is asked to respond.

Should the prize be one part or two? If two, can a mature method and an early clinical field be explained as one coherent prize, and which pairing is most defensible: B011 with B008 (Linke), or B027 with B008 (Brzezinski)?
Do any members who preferred another candidate in round 1 (Aili, Sparr, Aqvist) now rank B011 or B008 above their own preference, and on what grounds?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows two achievements with three explicit supporters each (B011 and B008), a single-prize B016 with two supporters, and single supporters for B009 and B027. Only Linke prefers B011 and B008 together, and the supporter sets for B011 and B008 do not otherwise overlap. A majority of five is not reached by any single configuration at this stage, and the open points are mainly attribution, overlap with the 2010 and 2020 prizes, and clinical maturity. The count is based only on the explicit round-1 configurations.
